page: Amazon Web Services m8g.metal-24xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by the 64-bit ARMv9 architecture. The system integrates an AWS Neoverse-V2 processor delivering 96 dedicated physical cores running at a base clock of 2.8 GHz, with single-threaded execution per core. Memory capacity totals 384 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM, establishing a balanced 4 GB per core allocation. The hardware platform includes no local disk storage, necessitating external network-attached volumes, while offering a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps without bundled GPUs.

In multi-threaded benchmarks, the instance demonstrates exceptional scale. Tests measuring stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, PassMark database operations, and Geekbench multi-core throughput place the platform within the top tier. Memory bandwidth tests for both cached read operations and large uncached read and write streams consistently reach top-tier percentiles. Conversely, single-core metrics across stress-ng and Geekbench register within the middle 50 percent range, indicating that raw aggregate parallel capacity exceeds individual per-thread clock throughput.

Qualitatively, the 96-core Graviton architecture delivers strong operational cost efficiency for parallelized enterprise tasks due to high core density and modern DDR5 memory channels. However, running without attached local storage requires reliance on network block storage, and single-threaded operations or unoptimized x86-dependent binaries present trade-offs against native high-frequency platforms.

The platform is well suited for highly parallelized multi-threaded workloads, including large-scale software compilation, in-memory caching systems such as Redis, high-throughput static web serving, container orchestration nodes, and distributed microservice architectures.

The instance includes no bundled GPUs and provides no local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions. Without local drive infrastructure, operational efficiency relies on balanced per-core resource allocation and low-overhead bare-metal execution. The server fits high-concurrency environments, including container clusters, distributed web serving, Redis caching tiers, Clang build farms, and parallel database backends.
